items: `identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`$id` updated to `https://gsa-share-it.github.io/code-json-schema.json` (reflecting the repository's move from the `DSACMS` org to `GSA-SHARE-IT`).
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
`identifier` added to `required`.
`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, `date`, `description`, `laborHours`, `languages`, `tags`, and `vcs` removed from `required` (now optional).
`feedbackMechanism` (singular)

`version`, `homepageURL`, `downloadURL`, `disclaimerURL`, `disclaimerText`, `relatedCode`, `reusedCode`, `partners` added as optional fields, taken from original [M-16-21 code.json schema](https://github.com/GSA/code-gov-data/tree/master/schemas)
`AIUseCaseID` added for assisting with agency collection of their AI Use Case Inventory as part of M-25-21 compliance
`SBOM` added to include software's SBOM in metadata as part of EO 14028

`categories`, `feedbackMechanisms` (plural, replaced by singular `feedbackMechanism`), `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, `softwareType` — these agency-extension-style fields were dropped from the generic gov-wide schema.
Migrated `$schema` dialect from `draft-04` to `2020-12` and introduced a formal `$id` (`https://dsacms.github.io/code-json-schema.json`).

Corrected the same structural bug present in `gov-schema-1.0.0.json`, where all field definitions were incorrectly nested one level too deep under a top-level `items` key instead of directly under `properties`.
`permissions.usageType` changed from a single `string` value to an `array` of strings, allowing multiple exemption reasons to be declared simultaneously.

Expanded and refined the exemption enum taxonomy: the old `exemptByLaw` was split into `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByNationalIntelligence`, `exemptByFOIA`, `exemptByEAR`, `exemptByITAR`, `exemptByTSA`, and `exemptByClassifiedInformation`; the old `exemptByNationalSecurity` (covering national security, confidentiality, _and_ individual privacy risk) was split so privacy risk became its own value, `exemptByPrivacyRisk`; `exemptByIPRestriction` was also added.

`organization`: removed the CMS-specific enum restriction (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`) and generalized it to a free-text string with an example (`'18F'` or `'Navy'`) suitable for any agency.
Top-level `additionalProperties` changed from `false` to `true`, allowing agencies to extend the schema with their own custom fields.

`AIUseCaseID`, `SBOM`, and `feedbackMechanism` added to `required`; `categories`, `feedbackMechanisms`, `localisation`, `longDescription`, `platforms`, and `softwareType` removed from `required` (dropped entirely, see Removed above).
Field definitions are nested one level too deep under `properties.items` instead of directly under `properties` (the same structural bug present in the CMS schema's `schema-0.0.0.json`).

`permissions.usageType` is a single `string` value (not an array), so only one exemption reason could be declared per release, with a smaller 8-value exemption enum (`openSource`, `governmentWideReuse`, `exemptByLaw`, `exemptByNationalSecurity`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, `exemptByPolicyDate`).
`organization` was restricted to a CMS-only enum value (`Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services`), despite this being the generic, agency-agnostic schema.
`identifier` field — a persistent unique ID used to track an asset across renames/migrations. Added to `properties` (right after `name`) and to `required`.
`downloads` property added to `reuseFrequency.properties`, alongside the existing `forks` and `clones`.
`permissions.usageType`
enum: M-16-21 exemptions are removed from the schema: `exemptByIPRestriction`, `exemptByAgencySystem`, `exemptByAgencyMission`, `exemptByCIO`, and `exemptByPolicyDate`

enum: `exemptByDisposableCode`, `exemptByExperimentalCode`, and `exemptByCommercialSoftware` are added, reflecting the SHARE IT Act's exclusions for exploratory/disposable code and commercial/COTS software.
Updated the `usageType` description text to define and renumber all 13 enum values to match.

Reworded the `reuseFrequency` description for clarity: _"Measures frequency of code reuse in various forms such as forks and clones for repositories, and downloads for packaged and distributed software."_

feat(misc#311): add Help page and sign-in help (#769)

* feat(misc#311): add Help page and sign-in help

Signed-in Help page with a topic rail (Getting started, Your systems, The
questionnaire, Scoring, Roles and permissions, System Delegates for HHS,
admin-only For admins). Content is split CMS vs HHS on the user's
identity_provider and checked against current app behavior.

Contact card emails the Zero Trust team via VITE_HELP_EMAIL (repository
secret HELP_EMAIL); the button hides when it is unset. Help nav tab and a
signed-in footer link. "Trouble signing in?" dialog on the login page with
short CMS and HHS steps and no ZTMF mailbox.

* feat(misc#311): move Help beside the account menu

Help is a utility, not a workflow area, so it sits apart from the nav tabs, highlighted while on the Help page.

* fix(misc#311): give Help links the token color for 508 contrast

MUI's default link blue (#1976d2) is about 4.1:1 on the footer gray and failed the frostfall color-contrast check on every page. The footer and Help page links now use colors.primary (#1B4DAB, about 7:1).

* refactor(misc#311): drop the footer Help link

The header Help link is on every signed-in page, so the footer link only duplicated it. Footer is back to its main version.

* feat(misc#311): add NIST SP 800-207, EO 14028 and CISA cloud TRA references

Per review. Government-wide references, so both CMS and HHS get them. The resource link icon now flows inline so it follows the last word when a title wraps.

commits.message:
Migrate dashboard reads in Title and Home onto TanStack Query (#756)

* refactor(misc#359): read data calls and systems through queries in Title

Title fetched both lists by hand and held them in component state, so a
mutation elsewhere had to announce itself through a context setter for the
layout to notice. The reads are now queries in the domain modules, and the
deadline sort moves into select so no consumer repeats it.

The decommissioned flag is part of the systems cache key rather than a
refetch trigger. Toggling swaps between two cached lists, so clearing the
filter costs nothing. That changes how ztmf-ui#572 is fixed: its test
asserted the clear refetches the unparameterized endpoint, which no longer
happens because that list is already cached. Every outcome assertion still
held, so the test now proves no refetch occurs and keeps the regression
guard.

Both queries stay gated on the session loader. The effects they replace
were gated for a reason: an unauthenticated call 401s, and the interceptor
turns that into a misleading session-expired redirect.

onCreated is gone. Once the picker reads a query, the invalidation from
useCreateDatacall does the work and the callback was dead weight, so the
prop and its type go with it and its tests assert the invalidation instead.

setFismaSystems keeps its old signature but writes the query cache, and the
context's fetchFismaSystems is now an invalidation. Both are transitional
so this commit leaves every consumer untouched; they come out when the
announce sites convert.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* refactor(misc#359): fan the dashboard out through useQueries

Home fetched the per-call aggregates and progress by hand, merged them in
an effect, and pushed four derived maps into state. The fan-out is now
useQueries and the maps are derived, so the dashboard holds no axios call
and no AbortController.

A failed call still resolves to an empty list in its own slot rather than
sinking the batch, matching the per-request catch it replaces.

The trend read shares the fan-out's query key instead of building its own
URL. When the prior call is also switched on, the two collapse into one
request. A production trace on 2026-10-05 showed that duplicate going out
twice, and the test that guards it lives in the Home suite because that is
where the regression would be reintroduced; at the hook level both callers
use the same helper, so the assertion could not fail for its stated reason.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* refactor(misc#359): resolve a missing system through its own query

Both pages reachable by system id did the same thing: if the shared list
had loaded without the system, fetch it alone and push it into the list.
That needed an effect, an AbortController, a one-shot ref to stop retrying
and a flag to hold the spinner, in each of two files.

A per-system query replaces all of it. The list stays the first source and
the query is the fallback, enabled only when the list came up short. A
system that does not exist resolves to undefined rather than erroring,
which is what both pages already rendered a placeholder for.

The resets that re-armed the one-shot fallback after a save are gone too.
The query refetches when its key is invalidated, so a save that moves a
system out of the current view no longer needs the page to re-arm anything.

The pillar-scores suite needed a query provider, and one assertion there
was pinning the append rather than the outcome. It now asserts the system
resolves and that the page does not write to shared state to render. Its
mocked context was missing fismaSystemsLoaded, which left the new read
disabled and failed in a way that looked like the component.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* refactor(misc#359): invalidate instead of announcing writes through context

The detail page announced its writes by calling fetchFismaSystems off the
Outlet context, and the two add-system flows spliced the modal's record
into shared state. Both were component state standing in for the cache: a
splice shows whatever the modal returned rather than the row the server
stored, and the announce path had to be told which view mode to refetch,
so it could be told the wrong one.

Each site now invalidates. The decommissioned flag is part of the list key,
so invalidating the lists prefix refreshes both variants and whichever one
is mounted refetches under its own flag. Nothing passes the view mode
around any more, which is why the issoName test that pinned that argument
is reframed rather than translated. The target-maturity mutation invalidates
the lists as well as the detail key: the card takes its system as a prop
from `listSystem ?? detailQuery.data`, so covering only the detail key
leaves the old tier on screen whenever the system is in the list.

That removes the last readers of setFismaSystems and fetchFismaSystems, so
both leave the context type, along with TargetMaturityCard's onSaved.

Title's remaining hand-rolled read handling goes too. vocabularyQueryOptions
bundled suppressErrorNotification with the cache settings, which is right
for system attributes and datacenter environments, since both fall back to
the raw stored value, and wrong for OpDivs, where an empty list leaves the
system form's Save stuck for the session. Title worked around that with an
effect reading the query's error and calling notify. The options are cache
settings only now, the two that want silence set the meta themselves, and
useOpDivs sets a new meta.errorMessage and lets the cache boundary toast.
Fixed text is the point: parseApiError gives "An error occurred, please try
again later", which does not say that OpDiv pickers are empty and a reload
is the fix.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* test(misc#359): drop guards that the context removal made unfalsifiable

Several suites asserted `setFismaSystems` was never called, which proved the
page rendered without mutating shared state. That member is gone from the
context type, so the assertion can no longer fail and the mock it reads is a
field nothing supplies.

On the decommission failure paths the guard was load-bearing, so it becomes
the real equivalent: a write that fails invalidates nothing. Elsewhere the
surviving assertions already cover it and the dead line comes out, along
with the stale mock fields in eight other suites and a TitleDecommissioned
comment describing a refetch effect that is now a query key.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* fix(misc#359): invalidate cached scores after questionnaire write

Dashboard aggregates and progress counts operate under a default 60-second stale time and derive from user answers. Previously, missing cache invalidation caused returning users to view stale scores within that window. Because legacy behavior refetched on every component mount, this introduced a regression.

Introduced `useInvalidateScores` across both mutation paths to invalidate the entire `scores` query key prefix. This ensures dependent views invalidate properly, as diff and per-system aggregate queries do not key directly on specific system or data call IDs. Updated the four `QuestionnairePage` test suites to include `QueryClientProvider` wrappers required by initial query hooks.

* fix(misc#359): stop the detail page blanking on a refetch

Three faults in one loading gate. It waited on a non-empty list, but an empty one is real for a scoped user, so a deep link spun forever. It gated on isFetching, true for background refetches too, so every save swapped the page for a spinner and lost card edit state and scroll position.

A save that moves the system out of the current view also left the by-id read with nothing to serve, so the detail key is seeded from the list now. Three mocked contexts needed fismaSystemsLoaded.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* fix(misc#359): return null for a missing system, quiet failed score reads

TanStack Query rejects a queryFn that resolves undefined, so fetchFismaSystem turned a served {data: null} into a failed query and a retry: two requests for an answer the server already gave. Returning null is what the docblock had been claiming all along.

The score queries carry suppressErrorNotification now. The code they replaced logged a failed read, and without the meta the fan-out toasts on every dashboard visit.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* fix(misc#359): keep the dashboard up while scores load

loading meant "any read in flight", so switching another data call on replaced the dashboard with a spinner and unmounted FismaTable, taking the user's filters and sort with it. It now means every read is still on its first load, which is what the spinner is for.

useDashboardScores folds its results through combine, with the fold declared at module scope so its identity is stable. The returned object is now referentially stable too, so the maps the dashboard derives from it stop being rebuilt on every row checkbox.

An empty selection is not an answer either: before the data calls land there  are no ids to ask about, and the dashboard rendered every system unscored for a moment before flipping to the spinner. useDatacalls already reported when that read settled and Title was discarding it, so datacallsLoaded joins the other two load flags on the context and Home waits on it.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* fix(misc#359): test the add-system invalidations and stop the duplicate toasts

Review feedback on #756. The three add-system flows were converted to
invalidations with no test behind any of them, so deleting one left its suite
green. Home, Title and the OpDiv header each pin theirs now, which needed the
latter two to capture their EditSystemModal props rather than stub the modal
to null.

Undo had the same gap a plain save had: useAnswerHistory invalidated only the
revisions key, so the dashboard served the pre-undo score until the entry
expired. It drops the whole scores prefix now.

Restoring fismaSystemsError and datacallsError for the OpDiv dashboard during
the merge left both reads toasting on failure, beside the panel the dashboard
renders from those same flags. Neither toasted before the migration, so both
queries suppress it and report through the flag alone.

Also drops the duplicated @param lines on useFismaSystems and the issue
numbers from the decommissioned-filter test, which git blame already carries.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* fix(misc#359): hold the systems list through a toggle, purify the seed

The decommissioned flag is part of the cache key, so the first toggle had
nothing to serve and the list went empty: the header read 0 systems and the
table's environment options vanished, which trips its own effect into
clearing that filter. keepPreviousData holds the other variant's rows while
this one loads.

fismaSystemsFetchedDecommissioned describes the rows on screen, which during
the hold are the other variant's, so it reads the opposite flag then. There
are only two variants, so placeholder rows were always fetched with the one
not being asked for.

The default selection also stops scheduling setActiveYear from inside a
setActiveDatacallIds updater. Updaters have to be pure and StrictMode calls
them twice; the effect reads the current selection instead. Note the
StrictMode test added here does not separate the two forms, since the old one
reaches the same end state, and its comment says so.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#359

* fix(misc#359): show the new status right after decommission or reactivate

The list refetch drops the system from the current view, so the page falls
back to its by-id entry, which still held the row seeded from the list
before the write. Its invalidation ran while that query was disabled, so the
old status painted until the read answered. Both endpoints return the
updated system, so it goes into the by-id entry before the invalidations.

The new tests feed the page from the real list query; the existing ones mock
the context list and could not see this.

commits.message:
fix(misc#408): correct breadcrumbs, page size, and missing-system state (#746)

* fix(misc#408): correct breadcrumbs, page size, and missing-system state

Root breadcrumbs at Dashboard instead of a non-existent Home page, maintain OpDivs casing, omit structural crumbs that name no page (such as Admin or the questionnaire's system segment), and link the system crumb directly to System Detail. Standardize table defaults to 25 rows (Users previously defaulted to 100, Events to 50). Pillar Scores and System Detail now resolve systems through a shared `useResolvedSystem` hook gated on `fismasystemsloaded`, ensuring users with no accessible systems see a "System not found" message instead of an endless loading spinner.

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#408

* fix(misc#408): clarify not-found copy and crumb casing

* fix(misc#408): apply crumb overrides to the first matching segment

* fix(misc#408): show a retryable error when the system lookup fails

* fix(misc#408): stop permission toast landing on not-found page

By-ID lookups traverse the request interceptor, causing `403` responses to trigger a permission snackbar over the "System not found" view. This inadvertently leaked resource existence: valid IDs triggered a toast while missing IDs did not.

Using `skipAuthHandling` silenced the notification but also bypassed `401` redirects, not-provisioned handling, and CSRF token refresh logic. Introduced `skipPermissionNotification` to suppress strictly the `403` snackbar while retaining error tagging. Updated the hook catch block to execute outside of `finally`, preventing transient "Could not load this system" flashes prior to `401` redirects completing.

Additionally, Pillar Scores fetched scores based solely on ID, causing excluded systems to trigger queries and duplicate toasts; the effect now awaits system resolution. Updated the system breadcrumb key to target `:fismasystemid` directly, fixing an issue where routes like `/systems/05` rendered unlinked text.

* fix(misc#408): drop systems breadcrumb while preserving questionnaire crumb

The `/systems` route corresponds to no standalone page, resulting in breadcrumb trails like `Dashboard / Systems / ACME` where the middle segment was unlinked. Because the `Dashboard` already functions as the systems list, the middle crumb was redundant prior to the target system name.

Conversely, the `/questionnaire` segment lacks its own dedicated route but is retained because it provides necessary context. Omitting it reduced the trail to `Dashboard / ACME / FY26 ZTM / Identity`, leaving the active questionnaire context unstated. Added a test assertion to lock in this behavior until a dedicated questionnaire route is formally introduced.
